video_title: Karim Lopez is set to become the 1st player born in Mexico to be drafted | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Jorge Sedano
quotes.summary_phrase: Karim Lopez poised to be first Mexican-born NBA draft pick
quotes.excerpt: Meet 19-year-old Karim Lopez, a 6-8 projected lottery pick who most recently played professionally for the New Zealand Breakers.
quotes.quote: There have only been six players of Mexican descent to ever suit up in the NBA. Most recently, six-man of the year runner-up Jaime Jaquez Jr. of the Miami Heat. But Jaime was born in California, not Mexico, a country that's home to over 30 million NBA fans and has never produced a first-round draft pick. That is until next week. Meet 19-year-old Karim Lopez, a 6-8 projected lottery pick who most recently played professionally for the New Zealand Breakers before making history at this year's draft.

quotes.speaker: Karim Lopez
quotes.summary_phrase: Karim Lopez on the pressure of being a Mexican basketball pioneer
quotes.excerpt: I always thought of it as a given that I was going to make the NBA.

text_blocks.speaker: Marc J. Spears
text_blocks.text: Do you get a sense back in Mexico how excited people there are for this history that you're going to make?

text_blocks.speaker: Karim Lopez
text_blocks.text: For me, I always thought of it as a given that I was going to make the NBA, even though it's the craziest thing ever, especially coming from Mexico, right? It's only been what, six players? I hope my story helps people see that you have to believe in yourself and you can do it.

quotes.speaker: Karim Lopez
quotes.summary_phrase: Karim Lopez on learning from NBL veterans and professional preparation

text_blocks.speaker: Marc J. Spears
text_blocks.text: Australia, the league you played in, the NBL in recent years, it's LaMelo Ball, Josh Giddey, Sarr. Have you been inspired by what they did?

text_blocks.speaker: Karim Lopez
text_blocks.text: It's honestly a big part of the reason why I went there and it's a big part of the reason why players keep going there because it's a great program and it's producing talent. You play against grown men. It makes you, you got to adapt. I try to be like a sponge, absorb as much as I can from those guys that have all the knowledge. It's been great preparation.
